description: 🔴 **BLOCKING DEFECT — the canonical router cannot make a network call, and other repos' decisions depend on it being able to.** Verified 2026-08-11 against source: `apr_router.erl:216` ships `default_transport() -> fun(_Backend, _Payload) -> {error, <<"no live transport configured">>} end`; there is no `httpc`/`inets`/`gun`/`hackney` anywhere in `provider-router-erl/src/`; and **nothing injects a real transport** — the only `transport =>` site in the tree is the default itself. **This is NOT the same claim tasklist `69` corrects, and `69`'s wording invites the confusion**: the Rust port program `translation/crates/wire` declares ONLY `serde` + `serde_json` (no HTTP client of any kind) and `apr_translate.erl`'s own docstring says it renders *'An OpenAI-shaped request out to Provider's native wire: `{ok, Path, Body}`'* while *'recognised, reported, **never dialed**'* and *'the worker records an **undialed attempt**'*. So the port RENDERS a request; something still has to SEND it, and nothing does. `69` is right that the router reaches seven vendors' **wire formats** — that is coverage, not dispatch. The honest degrade is already built (a `pending-adapter` rung is reported and the ladder walks on), so the router is INERT rather than broken — but the always-completes ladder currently always completes at the placeholder. **Downstream this invalidates two decisions in other repos**: formant's image-ladder consolidation (2,386 LOC) targets this router, and D9 routes lugh's out-of-envelope finetune jobs to agora — neither can land while the target cannot dial.

userStories.title: Give the canonical router a real transport
userStories.description: The rendered `{ok, Path, Body}` becomes an actual dial. `69`/US-3 already records **`req_llm`** (554★ Apache-2.0, native BEAM, 21 providers / 1,205 models with normalized token accounting and USD cost) as *'the untried better option'* — evaluate it against a plain HTTP client, and prefer **`gun`** (947★ **ISC**, same maintainer and license as the already-used cowboy) over `hackney` (NOASSERTION) if a bare client wins.
acceptanceCriteria: A live transport is injected and the canonical router completes a real paid-rung call end to end against at least one vendor; the rung is recorded as DIALED rather than as an undialed attempt.

The choice between `req_llm` and a bare HTTP client is recorded with its reasoning. ⚠️ `req_llm` is 554★ single-org — a thin maintainer pool for a layer-zero dependency — but it is the only credible BEAM-native alternative to hand-writing 21 provider adapters, and ADR-0004 already rejected embedding LiteLLM in the BEAM (correctly).
The ladder/budget/cost layer is UNTOUCHED — it never touches provider specifics, which is exactly what makes the transport a one-module swap. `unpriced` must still never pass a ceiling.
The **always-completes** property is preserved and re-proven: the terminal placeholder rung still cannot fail, so a transport that dies mid-ladder degrades rather than aborting.
`default_transport()` no longer returns an error as the shipped default — or, if an inert default is deliberately retained for tests, the production boot path is asserted to inject a live one.
userStories.notes: The Rust port stays doing what it is good at — CPU-bound serde wire conversion in a supervised OS process so a panic cannot take down the node. This adds the sender, not a second translator.

userStories.title: Correct `69`'s wording so the next reader is not misled
userStories.description: `69` states the router *'reaches ALL SEVEN native-wire vendors … through a Rust port program.'* That is true of wire COVERAGE and false of DISPATCH, and the ambiguity is what let this defect sit unnoticed.
acceptanceCriteria: `69`'s description and the docs echoing it distinguish **wire coverage** (8 `(vendor,modality)` pairs the codec can render) from **dispatch capability** (whether anything sends the rendered request).
The `pending-adapter`/undialed-attempt degrade is documented as the honest reporting mechanism it is, not as evidence that dispatch works.

ROADMAP Phase B is re-ordered so 'widen the codec' (`52`) is correctly framed as breadth ON TOP OF a transport that must exist first — widening what a router renders while it cannot send is work with no observable effect.
A test asserts the router's own reported dispatch state, so 'can it dial' is answerable from the suite rather than by reading source.
userStories.notes: This is the documentation half, and it is why the defect survived: two true-sounding sentences that describe different things.

userStories.title: Unblock the two downstream consumers explicitly
userStories.description: The point of fixing this is that other repos are waiting on it.
acceptanceCriteria: The **image** and **speech** modalities are confirmed dialable end to end, because formant's consolidation replaces a working image ladder with this router and must not degrade it — `apr_backends.erl` already declares `paid_providers(image) -> [openai, replicate]`.
A short note in `docs/` states which modalities are live, so a consumer repo can check rather than assume.
Once green, formant's `61`/image-ladder work and any D9 routing claim are unblocked; say so in the notes so the dependency is traceable in both directions.
userStories.notes: Formant's tasklist should NOT delete its own registry until this story is green — a consolidation onto an inert router would silently break image generation.
